name: Handle Ambiguous Project Request
query: Update my research project and change the description to 'New research direction'
context: The authenticated user has access to several projects: 'AI Research', 'AI Research Archive', 'Robotics Research', 'Research Platform', and 'Physical AI Research'. The user has not specified which project they mean. The exact project_id is not provided.
expected_behavior: Recognizes that the target project is ambiguous
Uses get_projects to inspect accessible projects
Does not arbitrarily select one project
Does not call update_project while the target remains ambiguous
Asks the user which project they mean
Does not claim that the description was updated
success_criteria: The model asks the user to specify the intended project
The clarification includes enough information for the user to select a project
No unsupported or guessed project_id is used
The model does not falsely report success

additional_scenario.query: Update the project called AI Research and change its description to 'New research direction'
additional_scenario.context: The authenticated user has two projects named 'AI Research' in different project contexts returned by get_projects. Their project_ids and descriptions differ, but the user's request does not provide enough information to distinguish them.
expected_behavior: Uses get_projects to inspect the available projects
Recognizes that the name alone does not uniquely identify the target
Does not arbitrarily select a project_id
Asks the user to distinguish the intended project using available project information
Does not call update_project before clarification
success_criteria: The model refuses to guess between duplicate project names
No project is modified until the target is unambiguous
